生数科技把 Vidu S2 全量放出来了，发布当天网页就能试。S2-Avatar 做实时数字角色，画面提到 720P，对话中途还能塞参考图，让角色换衣服、换背景、拿指定物品；S2-Editing 对着摄像头或视频流，实时改风格、人物和场景。他们还试了左右眼空间视频，给头显看。技术报告挂在 arXiv（2609.11638），体验口在 https://t.co/03ZrWI2KJa 。

云知声发了 U2-Flash。稀疏 MoE，总参数约 266B，单次激活约 10B。港交所自愿公告和官宣里的数字：DeepSWE v1.1 拿 64.6，比自家上一代翻倍，也压过他们点名的 GLM-5.3-Flash 和 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813；SWE-Bench Pro 61.6，比前代高 10.5。Agent 任务迭代少 20%–30%，周期缩短约 35%，Token 消耗也少 20%–30%。限时六折是输入 6 元 / 百万 Tokens、输出 2 元；9 月 15 日到 30 日还能领 1 亿 Tokens 试用，已经上了云知声 MaaS。

NVIDIA 把 OSMO 开源了，Apache-2.0。它不训练、也不仿真，只管把仿真、训练、真机评测写成一份 YAML，按硬件类型调度到不同集群；官方说内部给 Project GR00T、Isaac Lab / Sim / ROS 那一套跑过，每天扛过上千 GPU 小时。仓库里带了 agent skill，Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 可以用自然语言写工作流。你得有 Kubernetes 才能把控制面架起来，本地 quickstart 也写了不适合当生产环境。

Ao Qu 等人把 Reef 开源了。推理按兼容接口接进去后，轨迹和反馈会留下来；后台按配方异步更新模型权重，也可以改 harness（提示词、工具、编排），过评估门禁再热更新，不用停服务。仓库在 https://t.co/DlRrR9B1Qf ，Apache-2.0。

每天用 AI 的人都在同一个地方烧钱：先随便写个模糊的 prompt，输出不对，再改，还是不对，第四次才勉强对上。这三次全是白花的 API 调用，一天五十个 prompt 你自己算算漏了多少。

有个 Claude skill 叫 prompt-master，专治这个毛病。它不是把 prompt 写更长，而是写更准，每个词都得有用，废词全砍掉。

一句话总结它干的三件事：
1️⃣ 先判断你要喂给哪个工具，Claude、Cursor、Midjourney、Codex 都认
2️⃣ 缺关键信息就追问，最多问三句，不啰嗦
3️⃣ 出一段能直接复制的干净 prompt

免费，白嫖党冲。

豆包大模型 2.1 Pro 发布 0915 版本更新，API 已在火山方舟全量上线。这次升级集中在四个方向：Agent 任务交付、多模态写代码、多模态理解、以及推理成本。

Agent 方面的改进

模型在需要多轮调用工具、联网查资料再出报告的场景里，强化了证据溯源和数据核验能力，幻觉明显减少。官方给的例子是金融投研：模型能自主拆解研究需求、检索数据源再建模分析，产出的底稿接近分析师水平。为了核实某车企财报里的一个说法，模型调度了 500 多个子 Agent、检索超 1000 个网页，还交叉比对了海事航迹、卫星影像等多源信息。这类"不采信单方通稿、多源交叉验证"的能力，对企业做尽调、出研报有直接价值。

多模态 Coding

这次最实用的变化可能是看图写代码。模型现在能直接读懂设计稿、图纸甚至操作录屏，把视觉信息转成前端代码。官方演示了一个场景：给模型一段录屏加几张草图，让它给一个没有文档的老 ERP 系统开发移动端页面——模型读懂了 28 万行 Java 代码，直接还原出可运行的移动端页面。

在代码仓库理解上，模型对开源游戏 Luanti（约 38.7 万行代码）做了自主修复测试，83% 的任务达到了可合并标准。对经常要在大型项目里定位问题、跨文件修 bug 的开发者来说，这个数字值得关注。

其他升级

多模态理解方面，视频推理能力增强，能在视频里定位证据、跨帧整合；图像理解在 3D 物体识别（CAD 工件、游戏引擎元素）和密集图文解析（工程图纸、财报表格）上有明显提升。

成本方面，图像和视频推理的 Token 消耗比上一代减少 30% 以上。

Alistair Pullen（Cosine CEO兼共同創業者）は、Machine Learning Street Talkの「アメリカがAIで独走するのを見ている」において、米国の輸出規制が英国独自モデルの構築に向けた契機になったと語る。

・Fableが突然使えなくなった際、Pullenは「多くの人と同じく愕然とした」と語る。
・Cosineは英国初となる主権LLM（国が自前で持つ大規模言語モデル）の開発を受託した。学習にはBristolにあるスーパーコンピューターIsambardを活用する。
・「彼らが数十億でやっていることを、数百万でどうやるのか」。Pullenの答えは、事前学習に特化した研究所ではなく推論重視の企業として、国の計算資源の割り当てと企業連合からのフィードバックを生かして戦うことだ。失敗が許されない状況である点も認めている。
・米国が自国より先を進んでいることで、初めて二流市民のように感じており、それが何よりも悔しいと語る。
・オープンウェイトモデルは、規模、アクティブパラメータ、データ量の面で最先端にはまだ及ばない。10兆という数字も取り沙汰されており、その規模になるとインターネット上の大半の情報を圧縮している水準になるという。
・MoE（専門家の混合）と高密度モデルの比較では、モデルの体感性能を実際に左右するのはアクティブパラメータだと指摘する。
・エージェント向けフレームワークの重要性は薄れている。現行のモデルであれば、ほぼbashを操作するだけで大半のタスクに対応できるという。
・低品質な出力を抑えるには、最終回答ではなく思考プロセスに報酬を与える。コーディング性能が向上したのは客観的に検証可能な評価があるためであり、センスのような曖昧な要素も段階的な評価尺度で検証可能にしようと試みている。
・コードレビューを実行時の検証に置き換える。仮想マシン上でバグを再現させ、エージェントにそれを実際に悪用させて脆弱性を立証する。
・Swarmは数百のサブエージェントを並行稼働させる仕組みである。Kimi K 2.6を追加学習させた自社モデルを用い、Pythonで機械式時計をコードとして記述するSDKを構築させた事例を紹介している。

I ran a detailed comparison between Fable 5.1, Astra, and SWE-2 in Devin to map out their strengths and weaknesses:

SWE-2

– Strengths: It explores territory other models never touch, looking at problems with a much wider lens. It picks up on subtle cues with very little context. You can trust it with minimal prompting, like telling it to delete something without worrying it might wipe out unrelated code. It has great discipline. When evaluating a problem, it targets the main pain point right away instead of wasting time on trivia. Its "what not to do" advice is genuinely useful and keeps you from spinning your wheels in solved areas. Unlike Astra, it avoids arbitrary, nonsensical refusals. It feels much more honest about what it can and cannot do.

– Weaknesses: It lags far behind its base model, Kimi K3, in UI sense, aesthetics, and design taste. It also tends to stumble on a great idea and then hesitate to actually ship it.

Astra

– Strengths: Pure tenacity once it identifies a bug. It simply doesn't stop until it solves the problem. In one test, Opus 5 gave up and told me to file a support ticket, while Astra kept digging until it fixed the issue completely. It shows real engineering creativity, picking tight research paths with concise, structurally sound solutions and solid recommendations. It also has a great sense of success probability and offers precise statistical qualification for tasks.

– Weaknesses: It tends to plan around small sample sizes and thin evidence. It gets bogged down in minor details instead of looking at the big picture and overall impact. It also struggles to synthesize ideas across different domains, overspecializing until the scope becomes too narrow.

Fable 5.1

– Strengths: The highest evidence accuracy by far. It reliably delivers on what it promises, unlike models that promise everything and underdeliver. It has strong design taste, clear recommendations, and a holistic grasp of the end goal. It weighs priorities accurately. It can also pivot your entire strategy convincingly without drifting off into irrelevant territory.

– Weaknesses: Its answers are dense and exhausting to read. Once it settles on an idea, it's hard to steer it away. Its research skims the surface rather than digging up rare findings. It can suffer from tunnel vision, sticking strictly to technical aspects while ignoring costs or viability metrics unless prompted.
Patterns and Behaviors

– Negation: Fable and SWE-2 set broad boundaries. Astra uses rigid negative rules that abruptly flip decisions when triggered.

– Stability: Fable and Astra are steady. SWE-2 can be inconsistent, sometimes generating an idea only to backtrack on it.

– Length: Astra is the most concise. Fable is the longest. SWE-2 sits in the middle, though it has repetitive filler that needs trimming.

– Main Risks: SWE-2 over-explores possibilities at the expense of verifying existing code. Astra loses the forest for the trees. Fable turns practical technical decisions into academic literature reviews.

– Standout Traits: SWE-2 wins on thoroughness, Astra wins on grit, and Fable wins on raw reasoning and persuasion.
Scores and Recommendations

– Scores: 

Fable 5.1: 8.5/10. 
Astra: 7.5/10.
SWE-2: 7/10.

– Pick Fable or SWE-2 if you want strict prompt adherence, clean execution, or deep mechanical logic.

– Pick Astra if you need precise verification evidence and relentless debugging.

– Scope and context: SWE-2 and Fable are tied, while Astra falls slightly behind.

This is an initial assessment based on tests in Devin, and I'll need more runs to map out the nuances completely.

Following MiMo-V2.6’s live RL run. Useful to see learning curves alongside sampling stats, queues, costs, and restarts!

The2B tokens per step is a substantial workload. What I’d like to understand is the compute allocation: at a fixed total budget, what produces the most improvement on unseen tasks?

A few questions this run brings up:

- More prompts, more rollouts, or better feedback?

The dashboard shows ~1,568 prompts × 16 rollouts per batch. Covering more tasks and exploring more trajectories per task serve different purposes. Grader compute adds another choice: when is it worth generating fewer trajectories and spending more on evaluating them? The best allocation may shift as the policy improves.

- What does agentic in-group credit assignment actually do?

Test cases and rubrics provide different kinds of feedback. I’m curious how the grader compares attempts within a group, and whether it assigns credit to whole trajectories, stages, or individual actions. The ablation I’d like to see is whether additional grading cost pays for itself through more efficient learning.

- Critic/RLOO choices also affect scheduling.

RLOO uses sibling rollout returns as a baseline, a learned value function predicts return from the current state. 

If advantage computation requires the full group, slow trajectories can delay it even in an asynchronous pipeline. A value-based estimator that permits independent trajectory processing could reduce that dependency, but adds critic inference, training, and estimation costs. Retaining an RLOO component may retain the group dependency too.

This is a design question, not a claim about MiMo’s implementation. The dashboard’s critic/* metric names alone don’t establish that it uses a learned critic.

- Throughput needs to be read alongside policy lag.

More trajectories per hour don’t necessarily mean faster learning. By the time a long-running task finishes, its behavior policy may be several versions behind. How the system handles that gap - and avoids systematically favoring short tasks - matters alongside raw throughput.

The comparison I’d most like to see: time and total cost to reach the same held-out performance, accounting for rollouts, grading, environments, and any critic.

Appreciate the MiMo team making the run visible. There’s a lot to learn from the intermediate behavior of a training system.

DeepSeek's Flash price cut hits Zhipu and MiniMax valuations

On September 10, DeepSeek released V4.1 Flash and cut API prices again. Off-peak cached input now costs RMB 0.02 (~$0.0028) per million tokens, uncached input RMB 1 (~$0.14), and output RMB 4 (~$0.55). Peak pricing is double. The company says the new model beats V4 Pro on performance, cost, speed, and total time, and plans to shift some Pro traffic to Flash after September 14.

Zhipu fell 10.34% that day and MiniMax 8.98%. Through September 11, Zhipu is down 33.64% for the month and MiniMax 22.98%. Both reported strong first-half revenue: Zhipu RMB 954 million (~$131.6M), up 399.7% year over year, and MiniMax $117 million, up 283.1%. Zhipu disclosed August ARR of about $1.6 billion; MiniMax over $800 million.

Yet Jefferies cut Zhipu's target price from HK$1,299.8 to HK$1,183.79 and lowered the API business multiple from 50x to 30x expected 2026 ARR. The bank also raised 2026-2029 revenue forecasts 37-119% and trimmed loss estimates. The market is repricing growth quality: Zhipu's two largest customers each contribute over $250 million ARR, at least 31% combined. If one reduces usage, annualized ARR drops immediately.

We'd argue the core tension is that Flash models compress the premium window. Zhipu raised API prices 83% in Q1 and still grew call volume 400%, but GLM-5.3-Flash costs one-tenth of GLM-5.3 while outperforming GLM-5.2. Cached input generates 50x less revenue per token than uncached. Independent model companies must now grow call volume faster than unit prices fall, and cut inference costs faster than list prices drop. That is a much harder race than the one investors priced six months ago.

h/t @TMTPostGlobal

정책 논쟁은 속도조절인데, 개발 현장의 선택은 비용과 배포로 기울고 있습니다. 중국 모델의 오픈라우터 토큰 비중이 9개월 만에 20%에서 55%로 뛰었다는 수치는, AI 경쟁이 정상급 모델의 발표 횟수보다 실제 에이전트가 어떤 모델을 호출하는지에서 먼저 드러난다는 뜻입니다.

텐센트 Hy4 프리뷰는 8월 28일 공개된 오픈소스 모델로, 총 7700억 파라미터 중 49억개를 활성화하는 구조입니다. 오픈라우터는 요청 수가 아니라 처리 토큰으로 순위를 집계합니다. Hy4는 이 플랫폼에서 18조 토큰 이상이 처리됐고, 코딩·도구 호출처럼 반복 실행되는 업무에 맞춰 배포됐습니다.

그렇다고 토큰 점유율이 곧 성능이나 매출 1위는 아닙니다. 모델마다 답변 길이와 토큰화 방식이 달라 단순 비교에는 한계가 있습니다. 미국 기업의 코딩 에이전트가 중국산 추론 모델을 호출하는 조합도 늘어, 국적보다 가격·지연시간·도구 연동이 더 직접적인 선택 기준이 되고 있습니다.

그래서 볼 건 규제 발언의 강도보다, 개발자가 실제 업무에서 어떤 모델을 반복 호출하는지입니다.
